## Why

A write tool's reply lists its check results under one heading, "Check results:". The results a change made go away are in that list too, as lines starting "Gone:" (`src/tools/check-results-reply.ts`). Each gone line repeats the result's saved text, which reads like a problem that's still there. Example: "Gone: Twelve is closed for the whole visit, on Saturday, May 22, 2027. You'd get there at 10:47 a.m., with 1 h planned."

Joe's small evaluation on 2026-11-03 tested this on turn 10 of the Bar Harbor session, where `update_stop` moved dinner at Twelve to 6:00 p.m. and the closure warning went away. Two of Phoenix's built-in judges, completeness and tool response handling, read the turn on Haiku 5.5, 3 runs each, so 6 runs per wording:

- **The reply as it is:** all 6 runs read the gone line as an open warning.
- **"No longer applies:" in place of "Gone:":** all 6 runs read it as open. Some read it as the change not applying, such as "the time change 'no longer applies' and the stop was not successfully rescheduled."
- **"No longer applies:", with the text in the past tense:** all 6 runs read it as open.
- **A line that says what the change did:** "Fixed by this change: the earlier warning that Twelve would be closed when you arrived. Before this change, you'd have gotten there at 10:47 a.m. on Saturday, May 22, 2027, when it's closed." Completeness passed the turn in 3 of 3 runs. Tool response handling still failed it, for other reasons: it saw only this turn, so it flagged facts from earlier turns as made up. Its explanations read the line correctly, such as "the tool confirmed it fixed the closure warning."

The line that worked stayed in the "Check results:" list. A section of its own wasn't tested. The line also changed several things at once: it said this change fixed the result, called it the earlier warning, put the problem in the past, and left out the old text's caveats, such as "this time may be too early". Which of these did the work isn't known.

In that turn, the coordinator itself read the gone line correctly, and didn't raise the warning. But it reads the same replies as the judges, so it can make the same mistake, such as raising a warning the change just fixed. Raised by Joe on 2026-11-04, in chat, while going through #65.

## Design

- [Tool design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/tools.md), section 2.1, the paragraphs "Writing." and "The tool builds its reply from what the write hands back".
- [Technical spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/technical-spec.md), section 5.2, "How to handle broken feasibility rules", and section 8.
- [Domain model](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/domain-model.md), section 4.8: what new, changed, already known, and gone mean.

## Open questions

- None.

## Do

- In `checkResultLines()` (`src/tools/check-results-reply.ts`), change each gone line to follow the line that worked. Start by saying this change fixed or cleared the result, call it the earlier warning or note, and give its saved text as what was true before the change, not as a problem that's still there. Keep the lines in the "Check results:" list, where the tested line was. Don't use "Gone" or "No longer applies", since judges read both as open warnings. The test rewrote the text by hand, but code can only wrap the saved text, such as `- Fixed by this change: the earlier warning "Twelve is closed for the whole visit, ..."`. Change the line for a reply with no results to match.
- Change what says "gone" to the coordinator to the new words: the line on check results in its instructions (`src/agent/coordinator-prompt.ts`), and any tool description that mentions them. Then run `npm run agent-views`, so the view files show the new wording.
- Change tool design section 2.1 and technical spec 5.2 to describe the new wording. The domain model keeps its term "gone", and the code keeps `goneResults`, since neither is read by a model.
- The implementer drafts the exact wording, and Joe reviews it in the PR.
- Check the drafted wording with the turn 10 test: put a gone line in the new wording in `NEW_LINE` in `phoenix-tutorials/run-evals-with-built-in-evals/gone_wording_test.py`, and run it from that folder with the tutorials' Python (`../.venv/bin/python`). It needs the local Phoenix running. The folder is gitignored, so the test is only on Joe's machine. Put the results in the PR's decisions comment.

## Done when

- A test shows a write that fixes a warning lists it in the new wording, not as "Gone:".
- In the turn 10 test, completeness passes in 3 of 3 runs with the drafted wording.
- The view files show the new wording, and `npm run check` passes.

## Ends in

A PR.

**Settled in:** the PR. Propose each answer in the PR's decisions comment, and Joe agrees by approving the PR.

## Why

A write tool's reply lists its check results under one heading, "Check results:". The results a change made go away are in that list too, as lines starting "Gone:" (`src/tools/check-results-reply.ts`). A model reading the reply can miss that "Gone" means the result no longer applies, and read the line as one more open warning. In Joe's small evaluation on 2026-11-03, judge models reading the coordinator's tool replies did just that: they skipped past "Gone" and treated those results like the rest. When the gone results were moved into a section of their own, with a heading that said they no longer apply, the judges read them correctly. The coordinator reads the same replies, so it can make the same mistake, such as raising a warning the change just fixed. Raised by Joe on 2026-11-04, in chat, while going through #65.

## Design

- [Tool design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/tools.md), section 2.1, the paragraphs "Writing." and "The tool builds its reply from what the write hands back".
- [Technical spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/technical-spec.md), section 5.2, "How to handle broken feasibility rules", and section 8.
- [Domain model](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/domain-model.md), section 4.8: what new, changed, already known, and gone mean.

## Open questions

- None.

## Do

- In `checkResultLines()` (`src/tools/check-results-reply.ts`), take the gone results out of the "Check results:" list. Put them in a section of their own after it, with a heading that says they no longer apply, such as "No longer apply, since this change fixed or removed them:". Their lines no longer start with "Gone:". Change the line for a reply with no results to match.
- Change what says "gone" to the coordinator to the new words: the line on check results in its instructions (`src/agent/coordinator-prompt.ts`), and any tool description that mentions them. Then run `npm run agent-views`, so the view files show the new wording.
- Change tool design section 2.1 and technical spec 5.2 to describe the new layout. The domain model keeps its term "gone", and the code keeps `goneResults`, since neither is read by a model.
- The implementer drafts the exact wording, and Joe reviews it in the PR.

## Done when

- A test shows a write that fixes a warning lists it under the new heading, not under "Check results:".
- The view files show the new wording, and `npm run check` passes.

## Ends in

A PR.

**Settled in:** the PR. Propose each answer in the PR's decisions comment, and Joe agrees by approving the PR.
